comparison: Strong agreement on CSD-evoked calcium waves (C2, C20, C22-C24, C26-C28, C93). Both evaluations find this observation convincing and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative characterization with sample sizes, while peer reviewers highlight technical execution and expected wave speed.

Both address methodological differences explaining discrepancies with anesthetized studies (C110-C115, C117-C119). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental testing, while peer reviewers SUPPORT the interpretation as plausible but note technical differences cannot be definitively ruled out.
Complete agreement on independence between sensitization and ongoing activity changes (C83-C84). Both evaluations find this observation well-supported and consistent with distinct mechanisms.

Strong agreement on the major sensitization finding (C4-C6, C62, C67, C70-C72, C74-C76, C80-C81, C90-C91, C124, C127). Both evaluations recognize this as a key contribution with solid GLM methodology. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive analysis across afferent populations, peer reviewers highlight mechanistic implications for migraine.

Complete agreement on locomotion and deformation parameters (C56-C61). Both evaluations support the finding that deformation parameters remain unchanged after CSD, recognizing this as an important control for interpreting sensitization results.

Strong agreement on ongoing activity changes in awake mice (C46-C51, C108-C109). Both evaluations recognize this as differing from anesthetized studies and find the quantitative characterization convincing. OpenEval emphasizes statistical details, peer reviewers note the contrast with prior work as important.

Divergent evaluations of acute calcium wave mechanism (C39-C40, C42, C101-C102). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate mechanistic speculation, while peer reviewers raise UNCERTAIN concerns about GCaMP6 pH sensitivity during CSD potentially confounding interpretation of the acute response.

Agreement on clinical relevance to migraine (C7, C92, C138). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of clinical connections, while peer reviewers SUPPORT this as an important mechanistic insight explaining migraine worsening with movement.

Both address methodological approach (C15, C87, C140). OpenEval provides comprehensive SUPPORTED evaluation of technical details and validation. Peer reviewers praise technical execution but note weakness in sex balance (predominantly male mice despite migraine being female-dominant).

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretation of calcium signals (C94-C98) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about GCaMP properties and neuropeptide release. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these mechanistic claims about the calcium signal nature.

OpenEval finds background and motivation claims (C1, C8-C14, C85-C86) SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and clear knowledge gap identification. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these introductory claims.
